Gay-Lussac demo
Compare pressure for equal gas volumes heated from low to high temperature.
Demo steps

elements: three side-by-side apparatus panels in comparison mode: left Low P, middle Medium P, right High P
left panel title text: Low P
middle panel title text: Medium P
right panel title text: High P
left panel bottom caption text: Hot plate off
middle panel bottom caption text: Hot plate on medium
right panel bottom caption text: Hot plate on high
three identical dark rectangular hot plate bases, one per panel
three hot plate top surfaces, dark on the left, glowing orange on the middle, glowing red-orange on the right
three circular heating element rings on the hot plate top surfaces
three small hot plate front switches or indicator dots, dark/off on the left and red/orange on the middle and right
three transparent cylindrical beakers with pale blue glass walls, elliptical top rims, side outlines, and visible bottom ellipses
three water baths inside the beakers with flat elliptical water surfaces
cool pale blue water in the left panel
slightly warmer cyan water with a faint warm tint in the middle panel
hot/boiling water in the right panel with dense bubbles
sparse small bubbles in the middle-panel water bath
many bubbles distributed through the right-panel water bath
no steam or only a tiny faint wisp in the left panel
a few pale steam wisps rising from the middle-panel beaker
vigorous multiple pale steam wisps rising from the right-panel beaker
three sealed round-bottom flasks submerged in the water baths, each with a spherical bulb and narrow vertical neck
three translucent flask glass outlines in light lavender-gray
three black Gas labels centered on the front of the spherical flask bulbs
three vertical connector tubes rising from the flask necks to the pressure gauges
three small collars or gaskets between flask necks and gauge stems
three circular pressure gauges above the flask necks, each with black outer rim, gray inner rim, white face, central pivot dot, and tick marks
left pressure gauge needle deflected to a low reading on the left side of the dial
middle pressure gauge needle deflected to an intermediate reading near the center of the dial
right pressure gauge needle deflected to the highest reading on the right side of the dial
optional faint panel boundary rectangles or spacing guides to keep the three apparatus drawings visually separated

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The same sealed, rigid flask is shown at three temperatures; as heating increases from left to right, the pressure gauge reading rises while volume and amount of gas remain unchanged.

demo_steps.title: Compare all three panels
demo_steps.narration: The full textbook layout appears side by side: Low P with the plate off, Medium P with moderate heating, and High P with vigorous heating. The only intended progression is increasing temperature, and the gauge needle rises across the three panels.

demo_steps.title: Low pressure: hot plate off
demo_steps.narration: In the cool-water panel, the hot plate is dark and the gauge needle sits at the low-pressure reading. The sealed flask has the same size and gas label as in the other panels.

demo_steps.title: Medium pressure: hot plate on medium
demo_steps.narration: With moderate heating, the hot plate glows orange and the water shows mild warming. The flask volume is unchanged, but the gauge needle moves to an intermediate pressure.

demo_steps.title: High pressure: hot plate on high
demo_steps.narration: With high heating, the plate glows red-orange, the water boils, and steam rises. The rigid flask still does not expand, so the higher temperature appears as the highest gauge reading.

plan.geometry_notes: Use a flat, front-facing textbook-illustration layout with no perspective convergence and no extra graph. In three-panel comparison mode, arrange panel centers at X=-4.2, 0, and +4.2 world units, with each panel occupying about 3.4 units width by 5.2 units height. In single-panel modes, place the selected panel at X=0 and scale it about 1.45× while hiding the other two panels. Coordinates: +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z only shallow depth for glass transparency; keep all major silhouettes in the XY plane. Per panel apparatus proportions: hot plate base about 2.7 X × 0.38 Y × 1.15 Z, centered at local Y=0.35, dark gray #4b5656 with darker front face #333b3b; top surface is a shallow ellipse/rounded rectangle behind the front face. Heating ring on top at local Y=0.62, radius about 0.78 X by 0.22 Y as a flat ellipse; left ring nearly black #262b2b, middle #f28a2e, right #ff3b12. Beaker centered on the hot plate, local bottom Y=0.7, top rim Y=2.95, width about 1.75 X, height about 2.25 Y, shallow depth about 0.75 Z; glass pale cyan #bfeff0 at 0.25 opacity with darker cyan outlines #74aeb2. Draw the beaker as front/back ellipses plus two vertical side outlines; top rim ellipse width 1.85 X by 0.34 Y. Water fill inside beaker: surface ellipse at local Y=2.25 for all panels to emphasize constant bath geometry; color left #9fe6f2 opacity 0.45, middle #8fe6e8 with faint warm tint #ffd49b near bottom, right #8adff0 with many white/cyan bubbles. Round-bottom flask inside beaker: bulb circle/sphere radius about 0.62 centered at local (0,1.58), neck rectangle/cylinder width 0.22 X from local Y=2.05 to 3.35; glass outline #9da1aa, fill #d9d8ee opacity 0.35. The bulb must be the same radius in all three panels; do not expand it at high pressure. Gas label: black, centered on bulb at local Y=1.58. Connector tube above neck: width 0.10 X from local Y=3.25 to 3.62, gray #6c6c6c. Pressure gauge centered at local (0,4.05), radius 0.48; outer rim black #202020, inner rim gray #666666, face white #ffffff, tick marks black. Gauge needle length about 0.34; low-pressure angle points down-left about -45 degrees from vertical down, medium points nearly straight down or slightly right of center, high points down-right about +45 degrees from vertical down. Labels: panel titles at local Y=4.75 in black, captions at local Y=-0.15 in black; use simple sans-serif text. Steam: middle panel 3-5 pale cyan curved wisps from local Y=2.95 to about 3.55; right panel 10-14 taller wisps from local Y=2.95 to about 4.05; left none or one extremely faint wisp. Bubbles: middle panel about 8 small circles mostly near bottom and around flask; right panel about 30 small circles of varied radius 0.025-0.06 throughout water; left no boiling bubbles. Core correctness: the figure illustrates Gay-Lussac's law qualitatively, P proportional to absolute T for fixed n and fixed V, but do not add a P-T graph or numerical pressure scale because they are not present in the source.
plan.notes: Render as an orthographic, front-facing 2.5D illustration even though Three.js geometry may use shallow cylinders and transparent surfaces. Keep panel spacing wide enough that labels do not overlap. Use grouped objects for each panel so the panelView toggle can either show all three groups at equal scale or show one selected group enlarged. Do not include animated gas molecules, collision flashes, a P-T graph, or mini reference gauges. Use transparent materials with depth sorting disabled or outlines drawn last so the flask remains readable inside the beaker.

authoredPrompt: This figure shows three side-by-side panels, each depicting the same sealed round-bottom flask labeled "Gas" submerged in a water bath on a hot plate and fitted with a pressure gauge on top, together illustrating how increasing temperature at constant volume raises gas pressure. The left panel, labeled "Low P" and "Hot plate off," shows a cool water bath and a gauge needle deflected to a low reading; the middle panel, labeled "Medium P" and "Hot plate on medium," shows the hot-plate surface glowing orange, the water warming, and the needle at an intermediate position; the right panel, labeled "High P" and "Hot plate on high," shows the hot plate glowing red-orange, the water boiling vigorously with steam rising, and the gauge needle deflected to its highest position. Because the rigid sealed flask keeps both the volume and the moles of gas constant, temperature is the sole changing variable, so the progressive increase in gauge reading across the three panels directly demonstrates Gay-Lussac's law that pressure and absolute temperature are directly proportional. The visual progression from a dark hot plate and low gauge reading on the left to a glowing plate, boiling water, and high gauge reading on the right makes the monotonic P–T relationship immediately apparent. This figure establishes the direct proportionality between temperature and pressure for a gas confined at constant volume, motivating the mathematical relationship P ∝ T (in kelvin).
authoredInteractions:
- Toggle between the three heating states (hot plate off, medium, high): compare pressure gauge needle positions side by side and display the linear P-T relationship
- Slider for hot plate temperature: continuously update the pressure gauge needle from low P to high P in a merged single-panel view
- Animate gas molecules inside the flask: show them speeding up as temperature rises, causing more frequent wall collisions and higher pressure
authoredContext:
Imagine filling a rigid container attached to a pressure gauge with gas and then sealing the container so that no gas may escape. If the container is cooled, the gas inside likewise gets colder and its pressure is observed to decrease. Since the container is rigid and tightly sealed, both the volume and number of moles of gas remain constant. If we heat the sphere, the gas inside gets hotter ( ) and the pressure increases.

The effect of temperature on gas pressure: When the hot plate is off, the pressure of the gas in the sphere is relatively low. As the gas is heated, the pressure of the gas in the sphere increases.

This figure includes three similar diagrams. In the first diagram to the left, a rigid spherical container of a gas to which a pressure gauge is attached at the top is placed in a large beaker of water, indicated in light blue, atop a hot plate. The needle on the pressure gauge points to the far left on the gauge. The diagram is labeled “low P” above and “hot plate off” below. The second similar diagram also has the rigid spherical container of gas placed in a large beaker from which light blue wavy line segments extend from the top of the liquid in the beaker. The beaker is situated on top of a slightly reddened circular area. The needle on the pressure gauge points straight up, or to the middle on the gauge. The diagram is labeled “medium P” above and “hot plate on medium” below. The third diagram also has the rigid spherical container of gas placed in a large beaker in which bubbles appear near the liquid surface and several wavy light blue line segments extend from the surface out of the beaker. The beaker is situated on top of a bright red circular area. The needle on the pressure gauge points to the far right on the gauge. The diagram is labeled “high P” above and “hot plate on high” below.

This relationship between temperature and pressure is observed for any sample of gas confined to a constant volume. An example of experimental pressure-temperature data is shown for a sample of air under these conditions in . We find that temperature and pressure are linearly related, and if the temperature is on the kelvin scale, then P and T are directly proportional (again, when volume and moles of gas are held constant ); if the temperature on the kelvin scale increases by a certain factor, the gas pressure increases by the same factor.

elements: single merged apparatus panel showing one hot plate, one beaker water bath, one sealed round-bottom flask, and one pressure gauge
dynamic top title text: Low P, Medium P, or High P
dynamic bottom caption text: Hot plate off, Hot plate on medium, or Hot plate on high
dark gray rectangular hot plate base with slightly beveled top, front face, side faces, and two short feet
small front-right hot plate switch/indicator light, dark when off and red when heating
circular heating element ring on the top surface of the hot plate, dark when off, orange on medium, bright red-orange on high
transparent cylindrical beaker with pale cyan glass wall, elliptical bottom, thick top rim, and faint vertical side outlines
transparent cyan water bath inside the beaker with horizontal water surface
boiling bubbles in the water bath, sparse at medium heat and dense at high heat
pale cyan steam curves rising from the beaker, absent or nearly absent at low temperature, moderate at medium, vigorous at high
sealed round-bottom flask submerged in the water bath: spherical bulb, narrow vertical neck, and translucent lavender-gray glass outline
text label Gas centered on the front of the flask bulb
animated gas molecules inside the spherical bulb and neck of the flask
brief wall-collision flashes or ticks at the inner flask boundary when molecules hit the wall
vertical gauge connector tube rising from the flask neck
brown-orange collar and black gasket between the flask neck and pressure gauge stem
circular pressure gauge above the flask with black outer rim, gray inner rim, white face, central black pivot dot, and black needle
pressure gauge needle rotating from down-left at low pressure to vertical-down at medium pressure to down-right at high pressure
three small reference pressure-gauge icons arranged side by side near the pressure-temperature graph, labeled Low P, Medium P, and High P, with the active state highlighted
2D pressure-temperature graph panel to the right of the apparatus
graph x-axis labeled Temperature T (K)
graph y-axis labeled Pressure P
straight line on the graph labeled P proportional to T, V and n constant
three fixed graph markers for low, medium, and high temperature states
bright current-state marker that moves along the straight P-T line as the temperature slider changes

interactions.label: Heating state
options: Medium P / hot plate on medium
High P / hot plate on high
interactions.teaches: The three textbook panels are the same sealed flask at different temperatures; higher heating corresponds to a higher pressure-gauge reading.

interactions.label: Hot plate temperature
interactions.teaches: At constant gas volume and amount, pressure rises linearly with absolute temperature, so the gauge needle and graph marker move upward together as T increases.

interactions.label: Animate gas molecules
interactions.teaches: Higher temperature means faster molecular motion, producing more frequent and harder wall collisions, which is observed macroscopically as higher pressure.

demo_steps.title: Low pressure: hot plate off
demo_steps.narration: The water bath is cool, the heating ring is dark, gas molecules move slowly, and the gauge needle sits at the low-pressure position.

demo_steps.title: Medium pressure: moderate heating
demo_steps.narration: Turning the hot plate on raises the water-bath temperature. Molecules move faster, wall collisions become more frequent, and the gauge needle moves to the middle position.

state.heatingPreset: Medium P / hot plate on medium

demo_steps.title: High pressure: vigorous heating
demo_steps.narration: At high temperature the bath boils, steam rises, and the gas molecules collide rapidly with the rigid flask walls. Because volume is fixed, the pressure increases rather than the flask expanding.

state.heatingPreset: High P / hot plate on high

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a single centered apparatus rather than three full side-by-side panels. World coordinates: +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z depth away from viewer. Overall apparatus spans about X=-2.5 to +2.5, Y=0 to 5, Z=-1.4 to +1.4; graph panel spans about X=3.0 to 5.8, Y=1.4 to 3.4. Hot plate base: dark gray #4c5f5e top block about 5.0 X × 0.45 Y × 2.6 Z, centered at (0,0.25,0), with slightly darker front face #394a49 and two feet about 0.45 X × 0.35 Y × 0.35 Z under the left and right front corners. Heating ring lies horizontally on the top surface around the beaker base, radius about 1.55, tube thickness 0.08; color #24302f at low, #f0782d at medium, #ff2100 at high. Beaker: transparent cylinder radius 1.35, height 2.75, bottom at Y=0.65, top rim at Y=3.4, centered at X=0, Z=0; glass color pale cyan #c9f7f4 with opacity about 0.25, outlines #8fbfc0. Rim should be a torus/ellipse radius 1.42, tube radius 0.045. Water fill: cyan #67eee7 with opacity 0.45; surface Y about 1.75 at low, 2.05 at medium, 2.9 at high to match the source progression, with a flat circular/elliptical top surface visible through the glass. Round-bottom flask: spherical bulb radius about 0.9 centered at (0,1.75,0), neck cylinder radius 0.22 from Y=2.25 to 3.8, translucent lavender-gray #d9d8f1 opacity 0.45 with gray outline #9ca3a3; the bulb stays rigid and does not change size. Gas label: black text, centered on bulb front at about (0,1.75,front). Pressure gauge: face is a circle radius 0.58 centered at (0,4.35,0), oriented facing the viewer in the XY plane; black outer ring #202326 thickness 0.08, gray ring #55585a, white face #ffffff, central pivot radius 0.045. Gauge connector tube from flask neck top to gauge bottom: gray vertical tube radius 0.08, length about 0.5. Collar below gauge: brown-orange #b45b24 short cylinder/block with black gasket. Needle length about 0.43, black; needle screen angle relative to straight down is -45 degrees at 295 K, 0 degrees at 333 K, and +45 degrees at 373 K, interpolated linearly with temperature. Pressure model: P = P0 * T / T0 with T in kelvin, T0=295 K, P0=1.00 atm; thus low ≈1.00 atm, medium ≈1.13 atm, high ≈1.26 atm. Gas molecule count inside flask about 36 small spheres/dots, color #43a8d8 or dark teal, confined to bulb and neck; molecule speed proportional to sqrt(T/295). Steam lines: use pale cyan #aefcf4 curves rising vertically from the beaker rim/water surface; 0-2 faint lines at low, about 10 medium lines, about 25 high lines. Water bubbles: small semi-transparent white/cyan spheres or circles in water outside the flask; few at medium, many at high. P-T graph panel: white or very light gray background, axes black; x-axis covers T=295 to 373 K, y-axis covers P=1.00 to 1.27 relative units; line color #cc3333; low/medium/high markers gray, current marker bright red. Reference mini-gauges above the graph: radius about 0.22 each, placed left-to-right and labeled Low P, Medium P, High P, with the same three needle angles as the main gauge.
interactionPlan.notes: Render glass and water with transparency, depth sorting, and visible outlines so the flask remains readable through the beaker. The heatingPreset toggle should set the temperature slider to 295, 333, or 373 K; moving the temperature slider should continuously interpolate heat glow, water level/boiling intensity, steam density, molecule speed, gauge needle angle, and graph marker position. Do not instantiate the original three full panels at once; keep one main apparatus and use the three mini-gauges plus graph markers for side-by-side pressure comparison. Use instanced meshes or sprites for gas molecules and bubbles. Collision flashes should be short-lived small radial ticks on the flask wall and should occur more often at higher temperature. Keep labels as screen-facing text sprites so they match the flat textbook figure.

discrepancies: The source shows three apparatus panels side by side simultaneously, while the generated figure shows only one apparatus state at a time with toggles.
The generated figure adds a P-T graph, mini gauges, explanatory annotations, and extra UI-linked teaching elements that are not present in the source figure.
The initial view is an oblique 3D perspective rather than the flat front-facing textbook illustration, changing the composition substantially.
The hot plate, beaker, flask, and gauge are present but their proportions and positions differ noticeably from the source, especially the taller gauge/flask stack and smaller beaker footprint.
The generated low-pressure state includes visible gas molecule dots and collision effects inside the flask, which are not shown in the source low-pressure panel.
evaluation.notes: The apparatus and pressure-temperature concept are well implemented interactively, but the figure departs from the source by replacing the three-panel comparison with a single oblique 3D scene plus extra graph content.
action_items: Provide a default three-panel layout matching Low P, Medium P, and High P side by side, or add a clear comparison mode that displays all three at once.
Remove or hide the extra P-T graph and mini gauges unless explicitly requested, since they are not in the source figure.
Use a flatter front-facing orthographic camera view to better match the textbook illustration.
Adjust apparatus proportions so the beaker, flask bulb, neck, and gauge sizes more closely match the source panels.
plan_action_items: Revise the plan to prioritize reproducing the source as a three-panel comparative apparatus figure rather than an expanded interactive Gay-Lussac lesson with additional graph elements.

Gay-Lussac demo
Three fixed-volume gas samples are compared side by side.
Demo steps
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The rendered figure is much smaller than the source composition, leaving excessive whitespace and making the apparatus details hard to recognize at the default view.
Panel title and bottom caption labels are crowded/overlapping compared with the clearly separated textbook labels.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The same sealed, rigid flask is shown at three temperatures; as heating increases from left to right, the pressure gauge reading rises while volume and amount of gas remain unchanged.

demo_steps.title: Compare all three panels
demo_steps.narration: The full textbook layout appears side by side: Low P with the plate off, Medium P with moderate heating, and High P with vigorous heating. The only intended progression is increasing temperature, and the gauge needle rises across the three panels.

demo_steps.title: Low pressure: hot plate off
demo_steps.narration: In the cool-water panel, the hot plate is dark and the gauge needle sits at the low-pressure reading. The sealed flask has the same size and gas label as in the other panels.

demo_steps.title: Medium pressure: hot plate on medium
demo_steps.narration: With moderate heating, the hot plate glows orange and the water shows mild warming. The flask volume is unchanged, but the gauge needle moves to an intermediate pressure.

demo_steps.title: High pressure: hot plate on high
demo_steps.narration: With high heating, the plate glows red-orange, the water boils, and steam rises. The rigid flask still does not expand, so the higher temperature appears as the highest gauge reading.

plan.geometry_notes: Use a flat, front-facing textbook-illustration layout with no perspective convergence and no extra graph. In three-panel comparison mode, arrange panel centers at X=-4.2, 0, and +4.2 world units, with each panel occupying about 3.4 units width by 5.2 units height. In single-panel modes, place the selected panel at X=0 and scale it about 1.45× while hiding the other two panels. Coordinates: +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z only shallow depth for glass transparency; keep all major silhouettes in the XY plane. Per panel apparatus proportions: hot plate base about 2.7 X × 0.38 Y × 1.15 Z, centered at local Y=0.35, dark gray #4b5656 with darker front face #333b3b; top surface is a shallow ellipse/rounded rectangle behind the front face. Heating ring on top at local Y=0.62, radius about 0.78 X by 0.22 Y as a flat ellipse; left ring nearly black #262b2b, middle #f28a2e, right #ff3b12. Beaker centered on the hot plate, local bottom Y=0.7, top rim Y=2.95, width about 1.75 X, height about 2.25 Y, shallow depth about 0.75 Z; glass pale cyan #bfeff0 at 0.25 opacity with darker cyan outlines #74aeb2. Draw the beaker as front/back ellipses plus two vertical side outlines; top rim ellipse width 1.85 X by 0.34 Y. Water fill inside beaker: surface ellipse at local Y=2.25 for all panels to emphasize constant bath geometry; color left #9fe6f2 opacity 0.45, middle #8fe6e8 with faint warm tint #ffd49b near bottom, right #8adff0 with many white/cyan bubbles. Round-bottom flask inside beaker: bulb circle/sphere radius about 0.62 centered at local (0,1.58), neck rectangle/cylinder width 0.22 X from local Y=2.05 to 3.35; glass outline #9da1aa, fill #d9d8ee opacity 0.35. The bulb must be the same radius in all three panels; do not expand it at high pressure. Gas label: black, centered on bulb at local Y=1.58. Connector tube above neck: width 0.10 X from local Y=3.25 to 3.62, gray #6c6c6c. Pressure gauge centered at local (0,4.05), radius 0.48; outer rim black #202020, inner rim gray #666666, face white #ffffff, tick marks black. Gauge needle length about 0.34; low-pressure angle points down-left about -45 degrees from vertical down, medium points nearly straight down or slightly right of center, high points down-right about +45 degrees from vertical down. Labels: panel titles at local Y=4.75 in black, captions at local Y=-0.15 in black; use simple sans-serif text. Steam: middle panel 3-5 pale cyan curved wisps from local Y=2.95 to about 3.55; right panel 10-14 taller wisps from local Y=2.95 to about 4.05; left none or one extremely faint wisp. Bubbles: middle panel about 8 small circles mostly near bottom and around flask; right panel about 30 small circles of varied radius 0.025-0.06 throughout water; left no boiling bubbles. Core correctness: the figure illustrates Gay-Lussac's law qualitatively, P proportional to absolute T for fixed n and fixed V, but do not add a P-T graph or numerical pressure scale because they are not present in the source.
plan.notes: Render as an orthographic, front-facing 2.5D illustration even though Three.js geometry may use shallow cylinders and transparent surfaces. Keep panel spacing wide enough that labels do not overlap. Use grouped objects for each panel so the panelView toggle can either show all three groups at equal scale or show one selected group enlarged. Do not include animated gas molecules, collision flashes, a P-T graph, or mini reference gauges. Use transparent materials with depth sorting disabled or outlines drawn last so the flask remains readable inside the beaker.
